Task 4's own VALIDATE, check 1's second condition, runs `grep -qi 'settled by running' PRPs/prds/push-channel-proven.prd.md` — an unscoped, whole-file presence check — while Task 4's own ACTION gives the literal to write into the Decisions Log row for the success outcome as "`web-push@3.6.7` runs inside workerd under `compatibility_date 2026-08-01`; confirmed by [automated test / device pass]" (and the failure-outcome literal likewise contains no such phrase); neither authored literal contains the substring 'settled by running', so per R-COH-VALIDATE-PATTERN-UNGROUNDED condition (b) the pattern is not grounded in what the task's own ACTION instructs writing. Worse than a mismatch, the check is vacuously satisfied before Task 4 ever runs: the SAME file already contains the exact phrase via the PRD's own AC-11 ('... states that it was settled by running the library inside workerd rather than by reading about it ...', added by the 2026-09-07 amendment), so `grep -qi 'settled by running' PRPs/prds/push-channel-proven.prd.md` returns true today regardless of whether the Decisions Log row is ever touched. The writer's claim that this VALIDATE 'positively asserts the Decisions Log states the verdict was settled by running' is false as written — it asserts only that the phrase exists SOMEWHERE in the file, a condition AC-11's own prose already guarantees permanently. Fix: scope the check to the Decisions Log's 'Send library' row specifically (e.g. isolate that table row first — `grep -A0 '| Send library |' PRPs/prds/push-channel-proven.prd.md`, or an awk/sed range extraction of the Decisions Log table — then grep the isolated row for the phrase) so the assertion can actually fail when the row itself was never updated. Secondary, related observation on the same VALIDATE (not a second failing row, but bears on 'no always-pass path'): check 2's library detection is `if grep -q '\"web-push\"' package.json; ... elif grep -q '\"@block65/webcrypto-web-push\"' package.json; ...` — if a botched swap leaves BOTH packages declared, ADOPTED silently resolves to 'web-push' via the first branch and the leftover replacement package is never noticed, so the check does not truly enforce AC-11's 'exactly one send library ... is named as adopted' clause.
